about.title: Stockton Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Stockton sits at the crossroads of San Joaquin County, and its streets carry a steady mix of commuters, port traffic, and families running errands between Hammer Lane and March Lane. In 2025, public records show 1,313 injury collisions inside city limits, leaving 1,938 people hurt and 21 lives lost. Corridors such as El Dorado Street and Airport Way appear most often in those reports, and Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to see the heaviest concentration of crashes. Behind every one of those numbers is a person trying to figure out what comes next: how to get to a doctor, who pays for the car, and whether an adjuster's friendly phone call is really in their interest. LawProactive exists for that moment. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Stockton residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened; we handle the introduction; the attorney explains your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Stockton Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two Years Is Shorter Than It Sounds
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but claims involving a city, county, or state vehicle can require a formal notice in as little as six months. Connecting with an attorney early keeps those deadlines from slipping past.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame for a collision on March Lane or Airport Way; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No Recorded Statement, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement quickly, and you are not required to give one. Attorneys in our network handle that contact for you and work on contingency, so there is no fee unless your claim results in a recovery.

items.question: I was hit on Hammer Lane during Friday rush hour and the other driver's insurer already called. What should I do?
items.answer: Politely decline to give a recorded statement and don't sign anything until you've spoken with an attorney. Save the photos, the Stockton Police report number, witness contacts, and any dashcam footage you have. Friday afternoons are a common time for collisions in Stockton, and insurers move fast for a reason; you're allowed to slow the process down.

items.question: Does California limit how much I can recover for pain and suffering after a car accident?
items.answer: No. California does not place a cap on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in ordinary car accident cases. The amount depends on the facts of your injury and how well they are documented, which is one reason preserving medical records and evidence matters so much.
